'''Stephen Twinoburyo''' (8 January 1970 – 1 January 2019)<ref name=DM2/> was a Ugandan scientist, mathematician, lecturer, and entrepreneur. He was the [[Chief executive officer|CEO]] of Scimatic Solutions, a South African company which helps students with maths and science tuition.

==Early life and education==
Twinoburyo was born on 8 January 1970,<ref name=DM>{{cite news| url= https://www.monitor.co.ug/News/National/Body-Ugandan-mathematician-who-died-South-Africa-repatriated/688334-4918978-14weqsy/index.html| title= Body of Ugandan mathematician who died in South Africa to be repatriated| last=Tumushabe| first=Alfred| work=[[Daily Monitor]]| date=2 January 2019| accessdate=5 January 2019}}</ref> in [[Mbarara]], Uganda.<ref name=NV>{{cite news| url= https://www.newvision.co.ug/new_vision/news/1492028/uganda-mathematician-twinoburyo-dies-south-africa| title= Mathematician Twinoburyo dies in South Africa|last=Mubiru| first=Apollo| work=[[New Vision (newspaper)|New Vision]]| date=2 January 2019| accessdate=5 January 2019}}</ref> He was the second of seven children, and his father worked as a [[town clerk]].<ref name=DM/> He attended [[Ntare School]] and was [[Head girl and head boy|head prefect]] there in 1989.<ref name=DM2>{{cite news| url= https://www.monitor.co.ug/News/National/Twinoburyo-was-obsessed-with-maths-critical-NRM-leadership/688334-4922800-iy7b8qz/index.html| title= Twinoburyo was obsessed with maths, critical of NRM leadership| last=Tumushabe| first=Alfred| work=[[Daily Monitor]]| date=6 January 2019| accessdate=6 January 2019}}</ref>

In 1990, he started studying engineering at [[Makerere University]], and relocated to South Africa.<ref name=DM2/><ref name=NV/> During his time there, he was chairman of Lumumba Hall.<ref name=DM2/> He later studied mathematics as a [[Part-time learner in higher education|part-time degree]] at the [[University of South Africa]], completing the course in 2007.<ref name=AP/>

==Career==
In 1994, Twinoburyo visited [[Soweto]], South Africa,<ref name=NV/> and it inspired him to move to the country in 1997.<ref name=DM/><ref name=NV/> He lectured at the [[University of Pretoria]],<ref name=DM/> and taught in colleges in [[Pretoria]] and [[Cape Town]].<ref name=AP>{{cite web| url=https://www.africanpro.co.za/professionals/item/237-aupsa-chairman-stephen-twinoburyo| title= AUPSA Chairman Stephen Twinoburyo| last=Kundai| first=Keith|publisher=African Pro|date=6 June 2013| accessdate=6 January 2019}}</ref>

In 2008, Twinoburyo decided to found Uganda Professionals Living in South Africa (AUPSA),<ref name=DM2/> and worked as their chairman.<ref name=AP/><ref name="UD">{{cite web| url= http://www.ugandandiasporanews.com/2019/01/02/death-anoucement-late-stephen-twinoburyo-former-president-of-ugandan-professionals-in-south-africa-aupsa-suffers-heart-attack/| title= Death Announcement: The Late Stephen Twinoburyo: Former President Association of Ugandan Professionals in South Africa (AUPSA) Suffers Heart Attack|publisher=Ugandan Diaspora| date=2 January 2019| accessdate=6 January 2019}}</ref> In 2009, he organised a meeting of Ugandan [[expatriate]]s in South Africa. The meeting was held in [[Sandton]], South Africa.<ref name=AP/> AUPSA was set up to connect Ugandan expatriates living in South Africa.<ref name=DM2/><ref name=AP/> Twinoburyo also worked for the Ugandan Civil Alliance Network.<ref name=EWN>{{cite news| url=https://ewn.co.za/2011/05/06/Ugandans-in-SA-want-Zuma-to-decline-inauguration-invitation| title= Ugandans in SA want Zuma to decline inauguration invitation| work=[[Eyewitness News (South Africa)|Eyewitness News]]| date=6 May 2011| accessdate=5 January 2019}}</ref>

In 2010, Twinoburyo said that Ugandans were unhappy about the ticket prices for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]] in South Africa.<ref>{{cite news| url= https://www.pressreader.com/south-africa/saturday-star/20100605/281951719057130| title= Africa puts on its game face| last=Naik|first=Sameer|work=Saturday Star| via=[[PressReader]]| date=5 June 2010| accessdate=6 January 2019}}</ref> In 2011, he condemned alleged [[human rights]] abuses in Uganda, and asked South African president [[Jacob Zuma]] not to attend the inauguration of Ugandan president [[Yoweri Museveni]].<ref name=EWN/>

In 2014, Twinoburyo set up and became the CEO of Scimatic Solutions, a South African company which helps students with maths and science tuition.<ref name=DM/><ref name=Times>{{cite news| url= https://www.pressreader.com/south-africa/sunday-times/20140921/282746289980501| title= An office makes a perfect classroom| work=[[The Sunday Times (South Africa)|The Sunday Times]]| via=[[PressReader]]| date=21 September 2014| accessdate=5 January 2019}}</ref> He was inspired to set up the company after visiting the [[California Science Center]] and [[National Air and Space Museum]] in [[Washington, D.C.]]<ref name=Times/> The company is based in [[Hatfield, Pretoria|Hatfield]], Pretoria.<ref name=Times/>

==Personal life==
Twinoburyo and his wife had three children.<ref name=DM2/> He died in South Africa on 1 January 2019 of a [[heart attack]], one week before his 49th birthday.<ref name=DM/><ref name=NV/><ref name="UD"/> His body was [[Repatriation|repatriated]] to Uganda.<ref name=DM/>
